First, we find $v(t)$ by integrating the acceleration with respect to time:

$$
\begin{aligned}v(t) & =\int a(t)\text{d}t \\  & =\int (2t-5)\text{d}t \\  & ={t}^{2}-5t+C\end{aligned}
$$

To determine $C$, we use the fact that $v(5)=0.$ Substituting this into the above gives

$$
\begin{aligned}0 & =(5)^{2}-5(5)+C \\ 0 & =25-25+C \\ C & =0.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the velocity $v$ of the train at time $t$ is $v(t)={t}^{2}-5t.$

To find the time interval in which the train is moving to the *left*, we must solve the inequality $v<0.$ This gives

$$
{t}^{2}-5t=t(t-5)<0.
$$

Plotting the graph of $v(t)$, we get the following picture.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/differential/14094076/assets/afe458cdaf5eedbfb78cd9067b0c8caa209535391156bb5de14de34562f3cc1c.png)

From the graph, we see that $v<0$ whenever  $0\,<\,t<5.$
